old:
Proved in the verification document \cite{RigorCN5}; the argument compares the
pairs $(\omega,\widetilde\omega_s)$ and $(\omega,\widetilde\omega_{s'})$ for
$s\le s'$ through the semigroup law $h_{s'}=h_{s'-s}\circ h_s$ of \eqref{eq:hs}
and the monotonicity of root fidelity under the resulting compression.
new: \cite[Prop.~8.1]{RigorCN5}.  Fix $L$ and $s$, and write $I_i=(-a_i,L)$ with $a_1<a_2$.  The glued map does not depend on $a$, so by uniqueness of the normal extension (\cref{thm:normal}) the normal map on $\cF_r(I_2)$ restricts to the one on $\cF_r(I_1)$.  Root fidelity is monotone under restriction to a subalgebra, hence $\Phi(a_1s/(a_1+L))\le\Phi(a_2s/(a_2+L))$.  Every pair $0<\zeta_1<\zeta_2$ is realised by $L=1$, any $s>\zeta_2$ and $a_i=\zeta_i/(s-\zeta_i)$, and $\Phi$ depends on $(a,L,s)$ only through $\zeta$ (\cref{lem:mobius}).
reason: The proof was only cited, and the cited sketch (semigroup law) is not the argument of card phi-monotone-in-zeta (proved, rigor/check_note5_theory.tex prop:mono = Prop 8.1), which is the restriction argument now transcribed.
